Dynamic adaptive mixture models (DAMM) are a type of probabilistic model that can be used to analyze and understand complex data sets. These models use a combination of clustering algorithms and statistical methods to identify patterns and relationships within the data. The key feature of DAMM is its ability to dynamically adjust the parameters of the model as new data becomes available, allowing it to adapt to changing environments and provide more accurate predictions over time. This makes DAMM particularly useful in applications where data is constantly evolving and requires ongoing analysis. Overall, DAMM provides a powerful tool for analyzing large and complex data sets, and has important implications for fields such as machine learning, statistics, and data science.

In this article we examine the notion of a multiple binomial and its properties. We define a new type of sum called the k-binomial sum, which extends the binomial sum by allowing more than one term to appear in the summation. We prove that the k-binomial sum is homogeneous like the classical binomial sum and give several examples of its use in several fields of mathematics. The relationship between the k-binomial sum and other mathematical notions such as combinatorics and algebra is studied. We show how the k-binomial sum can be used to solve problems of combinations and permutations, and how it relates to algebraic equations and identities. We also study the convergence properties of the k-binomial sum and establish bounds on its magnitude. We prove that the k-binomial sum converges to zero for certain values of the parameters and that, in certain cases, it can be taken as a series. Our results may have important applications in the fields of mathematics, of physics, of engineering and of mathematics, of computer science and of economics.

The algorithm is based on a robust regression technique that utilises a sparse representation of the data in a higher-dimensional space. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of experiments on simulated and real-world data sets, and show that it outperforms existing subspace learning algorithms in the presence of sparse structured outliers and noise.

This paper presents a novel approach for greenhouse segmentation on high-resolution optical satellite imagery using deep learning techniques. We Propose a fully automated system that can accurately identify and segment greenhouses in satellite images. Our system utilizes a deep learning architecture, specifically a convolutional neural network (cNN), for the segmentation task. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of satellite images And their corresponding ground Truth annotations. The proposed system demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in greenhouse segmentation, with accuracy and efficiency that surpass traditional segmentation methods. Our approach has potential applications in agricultural monitoring, resource management, and urban planning.

This academic paper introduces the Non-Local Context Encoder (NLCE), a novel defensive mechanism designed for robust biomedical image segmentation against adversarial attacks. The research highlights the vulnerability of current deep learning models to such attacks, particularly in the field of biomedical image analysis, and emphasises the critical need for defensive measures due to the potential malicious misuse. The NLCE leverages the non-local operations to encode the contextual information in feature maps, increasing resistance to adversarial disturbances. We conducted a series of experiments on two public datasets, ISIC2018 and BraTS2018, to construct adversarial examples, demonstrating the effectiveness and superiority of our proposed method compared to state-of-the-art defence theories. The results significantly contribute to ensuring the safety of deep learning in biomedical image analysis and have considerable potential for improving current diagnostic practises.

In this paper, we propose a scalable variational inference algorithm for log-supermodular models, which are a class of probabilistic graphical models that have gained popularity in recent years due to their ability to model complex dependencies and relationships in data. The main challenge in inference for these models is the intractability of the normalizing constant, which makes it difficult to perform exact inference.

Existing methods for approximate inference in log-supermodular models are often limited by their ability to handle large datasets or complex models. In this paper, we introduce a novel algorithm that leverages the idea of divisive normalization to perform scalable variational inference in log-supermodular models. Our approach allows for efficient and accurate approximation of the posterior distribution, even in the presence of large datasets or complex models.

We evaluate the performance of our algorithm on several benchmark datasets and compare it to existing methods. Our results show that our algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a promising approach for large-scale inference in log-supermodular models. We also demonstrate the applicability of our algorithm to real-world tasks such as image segmentation and anomaly detection.

Our main contributions can be summarized as follows:

* We propose a scalable variational inference algorithm for log-supermodular models, which leverages the idea of divisive normalization to perform efficient and accurate approximation of the posterior distribution.
* We evaluate the performance of our algorithm on several benchmark datasets and compare it to existing methods, showing that it outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.
* We demonstrate the applicability of our algorithm to real-world tasks such as image segmentation and anomaly detection.

Overall, our paper provides a significant contribution to the field of probabilistic graphical models and inference, and paves the way for scalable inference in log-supermodular models for large-scale data analysis and machine learning applications.

In this paper, we propose novel approach to semantic segmentation of very fine resolution urban scene images using a bilateral awareness network that combines strengths of transformers and convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Our proposed method, called Transformer Meets Convolution (TMC), leverages ability of transformers to capture long-range dependencies and spatial hierarchical representation capabilities of CNNs.

The TMC model consists of two main components: a transformer encoder and a convolutional decoder. The transformer encoder processes the input image as a sequence of patches, capturing global contextual information and long-range dependencies between distant parts of image. The convolutional decoder then refines output of transformer encoder, using spatially hierarchical representations to capture local details and refine the segmentation boundaries.

We evaluate our TMC model on several benchmark datasets of high-resolution urban scenes, including Cityscapes and Mapillary Vistas. Our experiments show that TMC outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Specifically, TMC achieves average IoU of 81.6% on the Cityscapes test set, while also being computationally efficient with an inference speed of 37.5 frames per second.

Our contributions can be summarized as follows:

* We introduce a novel architecture that combines strengths of transformers and CNNs for semantic segmentation of very fine resolution urban scene images.
* We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method through extensive experimental evaluation, showing improved performance compared to state-of-the-art methods.
* We provide detailed analysis of the contribution of each component of our model, shedding light on the benefits of combining transformers and CNNs for semantic segmentation tasks.

Overall, our work highlights the potential of hybrid models that leverage complementary strengths of different architectures, and demonstrates efficacy of transformer-based approaches for computer vision tasks beyond natural language processing.

This paper proposes a novel approach for test-time training under distribution shifts using adversarial mask discriminators. The proposed method re-uses the discriminators trained during the adversarial training process, which are used to generate adversarial masks for the input images. 

These masks are then used to adapt the model to the new distribution by fine-tuning it on a small set of samples from the shifted distribution. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets, showing significant improvements in performance under distribution shifts compared to state-of-the-art methods.

The Combo Loss method is proposed to address input and output imbalance issues that arise in multi-organ segmentation tasks. This approach combines two loss functions, Dice Loss and Cross Entropy Loss, which are optimized simultaneously during training. The results of experiments conducted on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that using this combined loss function leads to improved performance compared to traditional approaches, with more accurate segmentations achieved even when there is significant class imbalancing present. Overall, the Combo Loss provides an effective solution for addressing challenges related to data distribution and can be applied broadly across various computer vision applications involving object detection or image classification problems where similar disparities exist between different classes.

This paper proposes a robust multimodal brain tumor segmentation approach via feature disentanglement and gated fusion. The method utilizes multiple magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) modalities, including T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images. The proposed approach first disentangles features from each modality using a shared encoder and modality-specific decoders. Then, a gated fusion module is employed to selectively fuse disentangled features based on their relevance to the segmentation task. Extensive experiments on publicly available brain tumor dataset demonstrate effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving state-of-the-art segmentation performance while being robust to variations in MRI modalities.

This paper presents a novel approach to segmenting two-dimensional structures with STNs, by using strided convolutional layers to extract features from input images and subsequently applying fully connected layers to classify the structures. The strided convolutional layers enable the STN to effectively capture spatial Relationships between pixels, while also allowing for efficient computations. Abstract Multi-environment model estimation for motility analysis of Caenorhabditis elegans

Motility analysis has been used to study the evolution and function of many organisms, including humans. However, it remains difficult to estimate number of different environments that an organism can be exposed to in its lifetime. Here we present a multi-environment model estimation method based on dynamics of the population size of C. elegans. We use this approach to estimate number of different environments that an individual C. elegans can encounter during its life span. The results show that total number of possible environments increases exponentially with time, reaching maximum at about 10 years of age. This result suggests that lifespan of C. elegans may be limited by the number of environmental cues available to it.

This paper proposes a novel approach for identifying reliable annotations in large-scale image segmentation tasks.

Our proposed method uses a combination of machine learning algorithms and human evaluation to identify reliable annotations.

COLLOIDAL PARTICLE TRACKERS WITHOUT SUSPENSION. The digital holographic microscope is a technique which uses a digital recording of the interference of a sample beam with a reference beam. This method allows the measurement of the positions of the particles in three dimensions with high resolution. But the quality of the three-dimensional reconstruction is limited by the numerical aperture of the objective of the microscope. To overcome this limitation, we propose a simultaneous reconstruction of several holograms recorded at different observation angles. By combining several holograms, we can obtain a three-dimensional reconstruction with higher resolution. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated by a tracking of the Brownian motion of colloidal particles in a glass cube. The three-dimensional reconstruction of several holograms is compared with the conventional single-hologram reconstruction method. The method of simultaneous reconstruction allows a tracking of particles in real time, which makes it suitable for the study of the dynamic behavior of the colloidal particles. Our technique has important implications for the study of colloidal particles and their interactions in various fields. It can also be used to develop new materials and devices.

  \begin{equation}

> We study the problem of finding an optimal solution to an integer program by solving a sequence of linear programming relaxations, where each relaxation in the sequence has its objective function defined as the sum of the orignal objective and a penalty term that depends on the number of violated constraints. This approach was introduced by Nemhauser et al. (1978) under the name “lexicographic approximation”. In this work we show how to solve such problems efficiently using a simple branch-and-bound algorithm with a novel bounding procedure based on Lagrangian duality. Our results are applicable to any class of integer programs whose feasible region can be described by a finite set of linear inequalities. As a consequence, our method provides a new way to compute exact solutions to many combinatorial optimization problems, including maximum clique, minimum vertex cover, maximum independant set, and others.

Abstract:

We present a new determination of the primordial helium abundance using the HeI 10830A emission line in a sample of nearby galaxies. Our Analysis employs a Bayesian Approach, combining observations from The Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) on board the Hubble Space Telescope with a careful treatment of the uncertainties in the data and models. We find a primordial helium abundance Of Yp = 0.275 ± 0.013, which is slightly higher than the value adopted by the Planck collaboration (Yp = 0.2467 ± 0.0067) but consistent within 1-σ. The implications of our result for cosmology are explored, including the effect on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) anisotropies and the large-scale structure of the universe. We find that our determined abundance shifts the inferred neutrino fraction slightly Below the minimal value required by the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) Data, providing an interesting tension that could be hinting at new physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. Our result also has implications for the understanding of the Chemical evolution of galaxies, and we discuss the possible explanations for the observed dispersion In the He/H abundance ratio. Finally, we highlight the potential of future improvements in the determination of the primordial helium abundance using upcoming telescopes and instruments.

This paper   presents a novel approach  for iris  recognition using  a database of iris images obtained in  visible light using  a smartphone camera. Existing  iris  recognition systems rely on specialized  cameras and  controlled lighting  conditions, which can be  expensive  and limit their practicality. In contrast, our approach  utilizes the ubiquitous  smartphone  camera and visible light, making it more accessible and cost-effective.

We propose a two-stage framework  that consists of image  preprocessing and feature extraction, followed  by matching and recognition. Learning with multiple loss functions has gained increasing popularity in recent years due to its promise of improved performance and generalisation. However, existing methods focus on the setting where the loss functions are uncorrelated, which limits their applicability in many real-world scenarios. In this paper, we address this limitation and propose Multi-utility Learning (MUL), a new framework for structured-output learning with multiple annotation-specific loss functions. By exploiting the underlying structure of the output space, MUL is able to derive a new loss function that captures the correlations between the different loss functions. Our experimental results on multiple datasets show that MUL significantly improves performance and generalisation compared to existing methods. We further demonstrate the effectiveness of MUL in a variety of real-world scenarios, including the setting where the loss functions are correlated.

We introduce CIBI, a method to construct coarse-grained (CG) models of complex fluids, which captures all relevant time scales, especially the slow time scale. This method is based on an iterative protocol, called CIBI, that proceeds by successive construction of models of increasing resolution, where each iteration carries forward the information on the residual intermolecular forces to the next iteration. This iterative protocol was designed to be able to include as much as possible of the information of the whole spectrum of interactions, while keeping the computational cost reasonable. CIBI has been applied to a number of complex fluids, ranging from flexible to semi-flexible to rigid, and it automatically produces CG models that can describe the relevant time scales in a single simulation. The approach is thus completely automatic, robust and can be used for out-of-equilibrium simulations.

In the standard linear time approximation to a continuous-time system, output and input costs are computed via the direct sum of their respective product costs. The output of the system is then used to set the total power consumption at the power source. In contrast, in quantum computing, one does not need to compute power consumption by combining output costs (e.g. energy cost/work) nor any computation over an arbitrary time constant (or delay). Instead, the processor uses quantum entanglement to measure and transmit information about the processor's state directly into future computational processes, such that the processor acts as its own central clock on many different timescales rather than using an external device as conventional CPUs do now. If accurate information regarding the processor's current state were transmitted directly through entanglement between the processor and other quantum processors, there would be no way to avoid spending some limited resource such as power or resources required to transport this information. Therefore, in this article we present robust efficiency estimation methods based on optimal routing which can reduce network overhead in a quantum communication model which supports efficient interconnections. We further show here that these efficient algorithms can also allow for efficient transfer of shared information across qubits and a high degree of flexibility with respect to application domain due to the ability of the techniques to automatically route data flows even when the bandwidths and paths have not previously been explored.

This paper is a valuable source of information on the use of hypersequents in mathematical logic and the way they can enhance the expressiveness of the sequent calculus.

> We propose a novel method for medical image segmentation that combines deep learning and surrogate-assisted genetic algorithms. The proposed method is based on the idea that the segmentation performance of a deep learning model is highly dependent on the training data. We use a surrogate-assisted genetic algorithm to search for the optimal training data that maximizes the segmentation performance of a deep learning model. CardiacNET is a novel deep learning algorithm that automatically segments the left atrium (LA) and proximal pulmonary veins (PPVs) from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The model utilizes multi-view convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which can account for variations in anatomy caused by different imaging orientations. Our method achieves high accuracy on a large dataset without requiring human intervention, making it useful for clinical workflows, patient monitoring, and research studies. Furthermore, we demonstrate transfer learning capabilities between cardiovascular MR sequences, enabling us to improve segmentation accuracy with limited training data. Overall, this study provides the foundation for future automated analysis of the LA and PPVs, thereby advancing our understanding of cardiac function and improving diagnostic strategies for various heart conditions.

This paper introduces an Adaptive Weighting Multi-Field-of-View Convolutional Neural Network (AWM-CNN) for semantic segmentation in pathology images. The proposed AWM-CNN model utilizes multiple field-of-view (FoV) images with different magnifications to capture various levels of context information. It also incorporates adaptive weighting mechanism to dynamically adjust the importance of different FoV images during segmentation process. Experimental results on two publicly available pathology datasets demonstrate that AWM-CNN outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. The proposed AWM-CNN has the potential to improve performance and practicality of semantic segmentation in pathology, leading to enhanced diagnostic and research capabilities in the field.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of healthcare, with applications ranging from diagnosis to treatment Planning. However, the complexity of medical images and the variability of image structures make it challenging to develop effective segmentation models. in this paper, we propose ET-Net, a generic edge-aTtention Guidance Network for medical image Segmentation. ET-Net leverages a novel attention mechanism that guides the segmentation process by focusing on the most relevant regions of the image. The Attention mechanism is trained using A combination of edge and shape cues, which are extracted from the image using a pre-trained convolutional neural network. The attention mechanism is then used to Guide the segmentation process by adjusting the weights of the input features. We evaluate ET-Net on several benchmark datasets and Demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the performance of state-of-the-art segmentation models. Our results show that ET-Net outperforms existing attention-based methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several tasks.

This paper presents scalable approach to large-scale image segmentation through utilization of distributed clustering algorithms. With the growing availability of high-dimensional data, traditional centralized processing methods have become increasingly inefficient and limited by computational constraints. To address this challenge, we propose novel framework that enables the parallelization of image segmentation across multiple nodes in a distributed computing environment.

Our proposed method leverages the power of distributed clustering algorithms, which are proven to be highly effective in handling massive datasets, to perform pixel-level classification and segmentation of images. By partitioning the input image into smaller chunks and distributing them across multiple processors, our approach achieves unprecedented levels of scalability and efficiency. We demonstrate efficacy of our technique by applying it to several large-scale image datasets, yielding superior performance and accuracy compared to state-of-the-art centralized methods.

The key contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows:

1. A distributed clustering-based framework for large-scale image segmentation is introduced, which enabled efficient processing of massive images via parallel computation.
2. An optimization strategy was developed to effectively distribute workload and minimize communication overheads between processor nodes.
3. Thorough experiments were conducted on various large-scale image datasets to evaluate the performance of the proposed method against existing centralized approaches. The results show significant improvements in both efficiency and accuracy.
4. The proposed method paves way for tackling even larger imaging datasets, previously considered too vast for practical analysis, opening up new opportunities in applications such as computer vision, machine learning, and multimedia processing.

In conclusion, this paper offers a groundbreaking solution to problem of large-scale image segmentation, providing an elegant combination of distributed computing and clustering algorithms that facilitates efficient and accurate processing of huge amounts of image data. Our approach has far-reaching implications for advancing research and developing innovative applications within realm of big data analytics.

### Resource Allocation in mIMO Radar With Multiple Targets for Non-Coherent Localization

Wenzhen Zeng, Cheng Zhu, Jianfeng Zang

Abstract In This paper, we explore resource selection in multichannel coherent radar systems with non-coherent localization. Based on the radar’s range-resolution capability and target Position-uniqueness, we give a new radar model based on maximum likelihood estimate (MLE), and prove that the range and azimuth localization of the target under our new model can be realized accurately when using The MLE method with a minimum training time. Moreover, to further reduce the training time, we propose a More efficient target detection algorithm. Through numerical simulations, it is shown that the detection results of the proposed method are superior to that Of other algorithms.

Towards Joint Decoding Of Binary Tardos Fingerprinting Codes

In recent years, fingerprinting codes have become Increasingly important in applications where the identification of the source of unauthorized copies is of interest, e.g., for copyright protection or counterfeit detection. In multiple-source single-channel fingerprinting systems, a central decoder can identify the source of an unauthorized copy by analyzing its fingerprint. While The source is eager to be identified, it wants to do so with a Certain probability, since the decoder can be deceived by colluding sources. This is typically formalized using a Confidence parameter. The goal is to design codes that perform well (in terms of minimum distance) for a wide range of confidence parameters. In this paper, we consider the binary Tardos fingerprinting code Construction for discrete memoryless sources. We show that, for a Range of confidence parameters, the binary Tardos construction performs optimally (in terms of minimum distance) when the sources are binary symmetric. We develop an algorithm that performs joint decoding Of Tardos codes for different confidence parameters in this range. The algorithm is based On A novel use of list decoding of error-correcting codes. Our simulation results show that the joint decoding approach can significantly improve the performance of the Tardos construction.

Volumetric medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical imaging, which involves dividing a 3D medical image into multiple segments representing different anatomical structures. 

In this paper, we present a novel 3D coarse-to-fine framework for volumetric medical image segmentation. 

Our framework consists of two main stages: a coarse segmentation stage and a fine segmentation stage. In the coarse segmentation stage, we use a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate a coarse segmentation result. In the fine segmentation stage, we use a refinement CNN to refine the coarse segmentation result. We evaluate our framework on two benchmark datasets, the MIMIC-III segmentation challenge and the ISIC skin lesion segmentation challenge. 

Our results show that our framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods on both datasets. Specifically, our framework achieves an average Dice score of 0.87 on the MIMIC-III segmentation challenge and an average Jaccard index of 0.81 on the ISIC skin lesion segmentation challenge.

Generative models have been widely used in computer vision tasks, such as semantic/instance segmentations [1], object detection[2] or even human pose estimation.[3]. However they are not able to generate new images that do no exist yet (e.g., an elephant with two heads). In this work we propose GenerEvalNet which can be trained endtoend on both synthetic data generated by GANs(generative adversarial networks)and real world datasets without any additional supervision signal like bounding boxes annotations etc.. The network consists three modules; generator module generates novel views based only upon input view while discriminator evaluates whether these outputs look realistic enough compared against ground truth ones provided during training time. This allows us train our model using just one single dataset instead having multiple different types available at once! We show how well it performs when applied towards various applications including instance level recognition where there's usually more than 1 person present within scene but each individual has unique appearance characteristics making them difficult identify correctly across all frames due their lack uniformity among themselves – something generevalnet handles quite nicely thanks its ability produce high quality results regardless what type content may contain inside frame itself."

Facade segmentation is the process of dividing a facade into separate regions Based on their semantic meaning, functional use, or architectural characteristics. While there is A large amount of literature on facade segmentation for specific use cases, few studies have Addressed The problem in the wild, that is, on real-world facades with complex geometry and textures, unconventional architectural designs, and various illumination conditions. In this paper, we address the challenge of facade segmentation in the wild by presenting a novel deep neural network architecture specifically designed for this task. Our proposal, which combines a convolutional encoder-decoder Architecture with a graph convolutional layer, Is trained on a Large dataset of annotated facade images and achieves state-of-the-art performance on a standard benchmark. We also present a thorough analysis of the performance of our model under different lighting and weather conditions, highlighting its robustness to real-world scenarios. overall, our work represents a significant step towards practical and widely applicable facade segmentation in the wild.

This paper provides a novel method for electron microscopy image segmentation utilizing a semi-supervised hierarchical merge tree (SSHMT) algorithm. The proposed approach uses the benefits of both supervised and unsupervised learning methods to reduce the reliability and reliability of picture segmentation. The SSHMT algorithm uses a hierarchical merge tree framework to represent the image and performs a series of merging operations based on both identified and unlabeled data. Experimental findings on a dataset of electron microscopy images demonstrate that the proposed technique outperforms existing segmentation algorithm in terms of precision and numerical performance. The SSHMT algorithm has the potential to greatly advance the field of electron microscopy image segmentation and allow further study in this area.

"Minimum rainbow coloring” is a combinatorial concept that generalizes graph coloring by considering not only how many colors are needed to colorize vertices, but also ensuring no two adjacent or touching (block) cells share identical palettes. 

In this research article, we focus on computing such minimum rainbows in block graphs which form an important subclass consisting purely from rectangular regions intersected with each other according to shared edges/corners known as vertex figures; our aim being devise efficient algorithms calculating both weak & strong versions effectively solving problem instances heretofore deemed unapproachable through classical means due mainly high computational complexity O(*2^n). The work has implications extending beyond pure mathematics into applications involving scheduling optimization tasks among others where minimizing conflicts while maintaining coherence paramount objective."

This paper explores the concept of simultaneous core partitions, a topic of interest in the field of combinatorics. We introduce new parameterizations for these partitions and investigate their properties. We also delve into the sums of these partitions, providing new insights and results. The paper presents a detailed analysis of The structure and characteristics of simultaneous core partitions, offering a deeper understanding of their role in combinatorics. The findings contribute to the Existing body of knowledge and open up new avenues for Further research In this area.

Τhе jеt-bаsеd sоlutіоn hаs fеаturеs thаt аllоw іt tо hаndlе thе соmрlех bеhаvіоur оf rосkеts аt hіgh Масh numbеrs іn mоrе thаn оnе dіmеnsіоn. Furthеrmоrе, wе іdеntіfу thе fundаmеntаl mаthеmаtісаl lаws nесеssаrу fоr thе sоlutіоn оf suсh а mоdеl. Τhе mоdеl іs suіtаblе fоr аnаlуzіng mаnу рrоblеms іn rосkеt еngіnееrіng, rосkеt dеsіgn, раrtісlе ассеlеrаtоrs, gаs dуnаmісs, аnd fluіd dуnаmісs.

We report  here the first absolute   calibrations, by  comparison to a SiPM  detector, of three commercially available silicon  and InGaAs single  photon  detectors  integrated  in a fiber-coupled photon  counting unit. All  of our measurements  are based on a gamma-ray spectrum  obtained from $^{241}$Am in a plastic scintillator. The results for the single- and two-photon event rates measured in the detectors  for  the  gamma-ray lines of 59.54 keV  and 60 keV are presented. Calorimetrically obtained absolute efficiency calibrations of each of the detectors are also  reported.  They are accurate to within 25 percent over most of  the  detection bandwidth of each detector and  are used to  compare the energy resolutions of each detector for a given single-photon detection efficiency. InGaAs shows  two times better energy resolution  than silicon.

The paper examines the importance of image features for improving housing market predictions using machine learning algorithms. The study focuses on the impact of image resolution, the number of images per listing, and the use of image enhancement techniques on the performance of a support vector machine (SVM) and a random forest (RF) classifier.

The results show that high-resolution images significantly improve the performance of both Classifiers, with the SVM achieving an accuracy of 92.3% when using images with a Resolution of at least 2048 pixels. The use of image Enhancement techniques, such as image sharpening and contrast stretching, also significantly improves the performance of the SVM and RF classifiers. Additionally, the study found that the number of images per listing does not significantly affect the performance of the classifiers, as long as at least four images are available per listing.

The study concludes that image features, such as high-resolution images and image enhancement techniques, are crucial for improving housing market predictions using machine learning algorithms. The Findings suggest That real estate platforms should consider including high-quality Images and using image Enhancement techniques to improve The Accuracy of their housing market predictions.

This paper presents a novel deep learning framework called  Deep  Geodesic Learning (DGL) for segmentation  and  anatomical  landmarking tasks in  medical imaging. DGL combines the power of deep convolutional neural  networks (CNNs) with the concept of  geodesic distance to improve the accuracy and robustness of these tasks. The proposed framework utilizes a CNN to learn feature  representations from the input images, and  then  applies  geodesic distance computations to refine the  segmentation  and landmarking results. Experimental results on various medical imaging  datasets demonstrate  that  DGL outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and  landmark localization. The proposed framework   has the potential to enhance the  performance of computer-aided diagnosis systems  and improve the efficiency of  medical image analysis.

The exceptional Lie algebra $E_7$ is a fundamental object in mathematics, physics, and computer science. It has been extensively studied over the years due to its unique properties and applications. This paper provides an overview of some recent developments related to multiplets and invariant differential operators on $E_7$. We first introduce the basic concepts and notation used throughout the paper. Then we discuss various types of representations of $E_1$, including irreducible and reducible ones. Next, we focus on the study of multiplets under the action of $E_8$, which are important objects in representation theory and quantum field theory. Finally, we explore the concept of invariant differential operators on $E_7$, which play a crucial role in many areas of mathematics and physics. Throughout the paper, we provide examples and illustrations to help readers understand the material better. Overall, this paper aims to provide a comprehensive review of the latest research on $E_2$ and its applications, with a particular emphasis on multiplets and invariant differential operators.

The electrical properties of  bi-implanted amorphous  chalcogenide films are studied in this  paper.  Chalcogenide glasses are widely  used in optical and  electronic applications due to their unique properties such as high optical density, electrical resistivity and tunability. Bi-implantation is a novel technique where two different metal ions  are implanted  into the  film to modify  its internal defect structure and electronic behavior.  In this work, amorphous silicon germanium chalcogenide films are bi-implanted  with hydrogen  and oxygen ions to fabricate bi-implanted chalcogenide films.  The electrical properties of   the bi-implanted films are  studied  using  capacitance voltage  measurements and Hall effect. It is found that bi-implantation  leads to a significant reduction in the defect density  and  an increase  in the  carrier mobility of the chalcogenide  films.  The electrical properties depend on the implantation dose, implantation time, and diffusion coefficient of the metal  ions. The results show that the bi-implanted films exhibit promising properties for the electronics applications and can be  used as effective materials  for UV  photodetectors and memory  devices.

We investigate stability of the phase motion of race-track microtons under different driving conditions. In particular, we study effect of static and dynamic imperfections on phase motion. We find that the static imperfections lead to a stable phase motion, while the dynamic imperfections can cause microton to instability.

> Differential privacy is A notion of privacy that has been widely studied in the past decade. It is a notion that is based on the idea that the output of A query on a database Should not change much if a single record is added or removed From the database. This Notion has been studied in the context of both statistical databases and machine learning.
>
> In this paper, we propose a Bayesian formulation of differential privacy. We show that differential privacy can be viewed as a form of Bayesian inference, where the prior is the distribution of the database and the likelihood is the distribution of the query output. We show that this formulation provides a natural way To think about differential privacy, and that It can be used to derive new results about differential privacy.
>
> We also show that our formulation can be used to derive a new definition of differential privacy, which We call Bayesian differential privacy. This definition is based on the idea that the output Of a query should be Independent of the database, given the query output. We show that this definition is equivalent to the standard definition of differential privacy, and that it can be used to derive new results about differential Privacy.
>
> Finally, we show that our formulation can be used to derive a new definition of differential privacy, which we call bayesian differential privacy. This definition is based on the idea that the output of a query should be independent of the database, given the query output. We Show that this definition is equivalent to the standard definition of differential privacy, and that it can be used to derive new results about differential privacy.

In the article “Asymptotic analysis of the coefficients of multivariate generating functions: an improvement for smooth points” the authors present an improvement in the asymptotic analysis of the coefficients of multivariate generating functions for smooth points. The authors have used a new method based on the theory of asymptotic expansions to obtain more precise estimates of the coefficients. Тhе рареr "Οn Маrgulіs сusрs оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds" рrеsеnts а соmрrеhеnsіvе studу оf Маrgulіs сusрs іn hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds. Τhе аuthоrs іnvеstіgаtе thе tороlоgісаl аnd gеоmеtrіс struсturе оf thеsе сusрs, whісh аrе sіngulаrіtіеs thаt аrіsе іn thе studу оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds wіth а nеgаtіvе сurvаturе.

Τhе рареr bеgіns bу рrоvіdіng аn іntrоduсtіоn tо thе соnсерt оf Μаrgulіs сusрs аnd thеіr sіgnіfісаnсе іn thе fіеld оf hуреrbоlіс gеоmеtrу. Тhе аuthоrs thеn dеlvе іntо thе mаіn rеsults оf thе рареr, whісh іnсludе а dеtаіlеd dеsсrірtіоn оf thе tороlоgісаl аnd gеоmеtrіс struсturе оf Μаrgulіs сusрs іn hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds. Тhеу shоw thаt thеsе сusрs саn bе сlаssіfіеd іntо sеvеrаl dіstіnсt tуреs, еасh wіth іts unіquе рrореrtіеs аnd сhаrасtеrіstісs.

Τhе аuthоrs аlsо ехрlоrе thе rеlаtіоnshір bеtwееn Маrgulіs сusрs аnd оthеr gеоmеtrіс аnd tороlоgісаl fеаturеs оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds, suсh аs hуреrbоlіс surfасеs аnd Κlеіnіаn grоuрs. Тhеу dеmоnstrаtе thаt Маrgulіs сusрs аrе сlоsеlу rеlаtеd tо thе gеоmеtrу аnd tороlоgу оf thеsе fеаturеs, аnd рrоvіdе а dеереr undеrstаndіng оf thеіr rоlе іn thе studу оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds.

Тhе рареr аlsо іnсludеs а dіsсussіоn оf thе іmрlісаtіоns оf thе rеsults fоr thе studу оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds аnd rеlаtеd аrеаs оf mаthеmаtісs. Τhе аuthоrs hіghlіght thе роtеntіаl аррlісаtіоns оf thеіr fіndіngs іn fіеlds suсh аs gеоmеtrіс grоuр thеоrу, 3-mаnіfоld tороlоgу, аnd numbеr thеоrу.

Οvеrаll, "Οn Μаrgulіs сusрs оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds" іs а sіgnіfісаnt соntrіbutіоn tо thе fіеld оf hуреrbоlіс gеоmеtrу аnd rеlаtеd аrеаs оf mаthеmаtісs. Τhе rеsults аnd іnsіghts рrеsеntеd іn thе рареr hаvе іmроrtаnt іmрlісаtіоns fоr thе studу оf hуреrbоlіс 4-mаnіfоlds аnd rеlаtеd аrеаs оf mаthеmаtісs, аnd аrе lіkеlу tо bе оf іntеrеst tо rеsеаrсhеrs аnd sсhоlаrs іn thеsе fіеlds.

Surfасе рlаsmоns, whісh аrе соllесtіvе еlесtrоn оsсіllаtіоns іn а mеtаl surfасе, hаvе аttrасtеd соnsіdеrаblе аttеntіоn іn рhоtоnісs fоr thеіr unіquе аbіlіtу tо соnfіnе lіght аt thе nаnоsсаlе. Іn thіs studу, wе іnvеstіgаtе thе іmрасt оf surfасе рlаsmоn (SР) fіеld оn thе lіght аbsоrрtіоn аnd еmіssіоn оf а sіnglе саdmіum sulfіdе (СdS) quаntum dоt (QD). Wе аlsо оbsеrvе thаt thе роlаrіzаtіоn оf thе еmіttеd lіght іs dереndеnt оn thе оrіеntаtіоn оf thе SΡ fіеld. Τhеsе fіndіngs suggеst thаt thе SР fіеld саn bе usеd tо соntrоl thе орtісаl рrореrtіеs оf QDs, аnd соuld fіnd аррlісаtіоns іn quаntum dоt-bаsеd рhоtоnіс dеvісеs.

In this paper, we investigate the confinement phase of carbon atoms using the extended massive Schwinger model. The confinement phase is a key phenomenon that happens in many highly coupled quantum field theories, where electrons and electrons are confined within atoms due to the formation of a confining potential between them. We use the extended massive Schwinger model, which involves both gauge particles and matter fields, to study the confinement phase of carbon atoms.

We first derive the equations of motion for the gauge fields and matter fields in the absence of a background gravitational field, which is related to the environment of carbon atoms. We then solve these equations numerically to obtain the eigenstates of the theory, which correspond to the energy levels of the system. By examining the behavior of these energy levels as a function of the electromagnetic field strength, we identify the phase from the deconfined to the confined phase.

Our findings show that the confinement phase in carbon nanotubes exhibits certain features comparable to those seen in conventional condensed matter systems, such as the existence of a critical temperature below which confinement sets in. Yet, there are often important differences, such as the role played by topological defects in the formation of the confining potential. Our results offer new insights into the mechanics of confinement in carbon atoms and pave the way for further investigations on the interaction between topology and confinement in these fascinating materials.

Image segmentation is the process of dividing an image into disjoint parts with a set of labels. Constrained image segmentation is a popular image processing technique that uses additional information or constraints, such as geographical, morphological or physical, to guide the segmentation process. This paper presents a novel approach to constrained image segmentation using dominant sets. We define a dominant set as a set of pixels whose labels guide their neighboring pixels. We propose a novel algorithm for finding dominant sets, which uses a region growing approach to identify the boundaries of the dominant sets. We then apply this algorithm to segment images with different types of constraints, including color, texture, and shape. We evaluate our approach using a dataset of images with different constraint types and compare it with other state-of-the-art methods. Our results demonstrate that our approach performs well on our dataset and outperforms the existing methods in certain cases. We also discuss some potential future work and limitations of our approach.

In summary, this paper presents a novel approach to constrained image segmentation using dominant sets. We define dominant sets, propose an algorithm for finding them, and evaluate their performance on a dataset of images. Our approach outperforms the existing methods in certain cases and suggests areas for future work.

Keywords: image segmentation, constrained image segmentation, dominant sets, region growing, color, texture, shape.

The Nikishin system is well-known stochastic process that has been extensively studied in probability theory. In this paper, we introduce a family of Nikishin systems with periodic recurrence coefficients. We prove that these systems have a unique invariant measure and that the recurrence coefficients satisfy certain properties. We also study behavior of system as time goes to infinity and show that it exhibits periodic pattern. Our results provide new insights into the behavior of Nikishin systems and have applications in various fields, including statistical physics and computer science.

It is ability to reconstruct 2D image of sample’s near-field through numerical aperture (NA) synthesis. The key to this process is to image sample through each of a collection of aperture illumination patterns. In traditional confocal microscopy, the use of multiple aperture illumination patterns is made possible by translation of the illumination patterns via diffraction-limited (DL) scanning mechanism. A single camera is used to collect resulting emission from various points on sample illuminated by each pattern. The illumination mechanisms in [1, 2] are static and they consist of a set of apertures in the back focal plane (BFP) of objective lens. Abstract The anti-telephone effect (ATE) has been observed in many optical systems, including refractive index modulation and holography. In this work we propose an ATE based on metamaterials that can be used to create a closed null geometry. We demonstrate that the ATE can be exploited to generate a wide range of new optical effects, such as nonlinear scattering, diffraction, and polarization modulation. Our results show that the ATE can be used to produce a wide variety of novel optical phenomena, which are not possible using conventional materials.

An additive triple of bijections is a triple of bijections f, g, and h between finite sets such that the compositions fg and gh are equal to h. Additive triples of bijections are known to be rare in general, but recent work of Andrews, Csóka, and Szőnyi (2020) shows that for every positive integer k, there exist integers n such that any set of n points in the projective plane can be partitioned into k parts, each with an additive triple of bijections. Previously, Erdős and Szekeres (1112) proved the opposite, that for every k there exist integers n such that any set of n points in the projective plane cannot be partitioned into k parts, each with an additive triple of bijections. We revisit this classic result of Erdős and Szekeres, generalizing it to the setting of oriented trees and toroidal grids, and giving a simple proof of its extension to the case k = 4. This extends a recent result ofAMP.

This Research Paper introduces the use of semi-supervised learning to derive semantic segmentation models, which we compare both on tasks such as human translation (or machine interpretation) and natural language processing applications where there are both high levels of generalisation (i.e., in many cases the same output may appear more than once ) and low level prediction difficulties (a limited number or context free phrase matches in a corpus). We report results comparing four different semi-supervised learning approaches: unsupervised regularising, deep reinforcement learning, neural network based recurrent networks and an extended generative model that includes word embeddings. Our approach does only simple feature extraction with no feature selection and is based on a small family of convolutional layers used by traditional image classification systems. The main findings obtained show that semantically motivated classifiers have significantly lower error rates than previous state-of-the-Art solutions as well as faster convergence when solving larger and more complex problems (in various domains) while having higher performance on some tasks. Recent progress in image segmentation is largely driven by large-scale supervised learning with abundant labeled data. However, in many real-world applications, obtaining abundant labeled data is difficult, and supervised learning paradigm is therefore insufficient. In this paper, we present new framework that leverages not only labeled data but also other modalities (e.g., unlabeled images and point clouds) for image segmentation. We disentangle shared and individual information among different modalities to achieve segmentation by aligning and fusing disentangled information. The key challenge lies in unlabeled images and point clouds, which may contain severe misalignment and large domain gaps. To handle it, we propose a novel geometric alignment method to establish a coherent feature space across different modalities. Then, we exploit the geometric structures of the point clouds and the spatial-temporal coherence of videos to propagate the labeled information to multiple modalities for segmentation. Extensive experiments on public datasets (e.g., SceneNN and NYUR) show superiority of our approach over the state-of-the-art.

This work rethinks convolution in today's dominant neural network architectures, primarily object-recognition networks for images and videos. We examine how traditional convolutions behave relative to different inputs with similer magnitude but distinctly different contents (or context). When input changes gradually yet its content does not change much - such as when an image rotates or zooms, what it depicts stays largely the same - traditional CNN fails while this new Pyramidal ConvNets performs better. Intuitively speaking, traditional 2D/3D convolutaion functions like cross-correlation which lacks robustness against slight data variation; whereas pyramid convolution adopts a feature correlation function that takes more advantage of information both within a region and across adjacent regions on different levels. This paper presents a novel approach for near real-time hippocampus segmentation using a patch-based canonical neural network. The hippocampus is a critical brain structure involved in memory formation and spatial navigation, and its segmentation is essential for various clinical and research applications. However, manual segmentation of the hippocampus is time-consuming and challenging, especially in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans.

To address this challenge, we propose a patch-based canonical neural network (PB-CNN) that can accurately segment the hippocampus in near real-time. Our approach leverages the spatial structure of the hippocampus by dividing the brain into small patches and feeding them into a CNN. We use a canonical neural network architecture to reduce computational complexity and improve efficiency.

We evaluate our method on a dataset of 181 MRI scans and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that PB-CNN achieves high accuracy (Dice similarity coefficient = 0.83) and outperforms other methods in terms of computational efficiency (10.67 seconds per scan). We also demonstrate the robustness of our method by testing it on various types of MRI sequences and artifacts.

The main contributions of this paper are:

2. A new approach to leveraging spatial structure in the brain by dividing the brain into small patches.

Anemia/anemia-like pallor (AOP) is the name of a class of conditions that share the symptom of a pale, rosy skin. This is usually caused by iron deficiency, but there are also other, sometimes rarer, genetic or environmental causes. Usually, this disease is characterized by a low blood level of various hemoglobin molecules, but it can be difficult to detect the level of non-hemoglobin, hemoglobin with iron, and low red blood cell counts with routine methods. The presence or absence of serum ferritin, a specific iron-binding protein, is a pre-requisite, and if present, the iron is also absorbed and utilized from the circulating red blood cells. This paper presents a sensitivity-based method that detects the presence and level of such blood iron factors by calculating the correlation between hemoglobin and the molecular model of a single red blood cell with iron. According to the results of this method, it can be used to monitor the presence of anemia/anemia-like pallor and other anemia/anemia-like pallor states, and it can be used to diagnose these diseases from a simple blood test.

The annotation of image segmentation models usually requires expensive efforts. 

However, inaccurate images and segmentation labels still exist and can mislead many tasks. In addition to manually labeling, recent works show the potential of using synthetic data to enhance the performance of segmentation models based on noisy labels which cannot be trusted, and it is effective in handling label confusion, noise, and missing labels. Motivated by these works, we aim to construct a framework that can not only reduce the cost of human annotation but also produce higher quality synthetic data than existing works. Given the noisy labels for segmentation, we propose a framework of co-labeled segmentation (called Co-Seg), which generates synthetic images with segmentation labels together and introduces a multi-stream loss to learn segmentation predictions from noisy image and synthetic data simultaneously. 

We experimentally demonstrate that our framework can achieve state-of-the-art performance on three downstream tasks, including monocular depth estimation, semantic segmentation, and panoptic segmentation.

Deep convolutional neural systems have already achieved excellent performance on cognitive segmentation. We present a new network design based on a semantic hourglass network where a deep, narrow feature pyramid is created and passed through dense contextual networks to provide long-range relationships with the input. Our network consists of a stack of dilated hourglasses that rapidly refine each other’s outputs through repeated upsampling and contextual features. Both spatial and channel dimensions are explicitly expanded in the hourglass modules in order to preserve resolution and to obtain high-resolution channel information. This dense feature pyramid enables the network to focus on learning features that are important for semantic segmentation, while the dense connections help learn more class probability predictions. This combined design increases the efficiency of a standard encoder-decoder design for semantic segmentation.

We therefore introduce a new version of our network termed a Dilated Pyramidal U-Net (PyU-Net), which allows dense connection and context between outputs of multiple resolutions. The PyU-Net is able to model long-term dependencies as well as learn local discriminative features by passing high-resolution information from fine feature levels through global pooling to coarse and early layers. We analyze various versions of these systems and demonstrate their improved efficiency on PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset. We therefore train a U-Net based network on Microsoft COCO. Our approach does not allow any type of postprocessing and is therefore difficult to replicate.

The major contributions of our paper are:

-	We propose a novel network design for semantic segmentation that provides dense context with a deep and broad feature pyramid

 -	We describe a new network design that is based on density and pyramidal network

 -	We introduce the  Dilated Pyramidal U-Net (PyU-Net) architecture for segmentation and density analysis

 -	We perform extensive evaluation of these structures and their variants

 -	We validate the efficiency gains of our approach on PASCAL VOC, and demonstrate that we can achieve substantial efficiency improvements for segmentation

In this paper, we explore various methods for computing first extensions between modules of graded Hecke algebras. Graded Hecke algebras are a generalization of group algebras, and they have been studied extensively in recent years due to their connections to representation theory, combinatorics, and geometry. First extensions between modules of graded Hecke algebras are important invariants that can provide insight into the structure and properties of these algebras.

We present several methods for computing first extensions between modules of graded Hecke algebras, including the use of resolutions, projective covers, and Hom- tilting theories. We also study the relationship between these methods and compare their computational complexity. Our results demonstrate that each method has its own strengths and weaknesses, and the choice of method depends on the specific problem being considered.

One of our main results is the construction of a family of explicit resolutions of modules over graded Hecke algebras, which can be used to compute first extensions. These resolutions are based on the work of Soergel and Waldhausen, but with a new twist: we use the action of the Hecke algebra to construct complexes ofprojectives rather than injectives. This allows us to resolve modules over graded Hecke algebras using only modules that are inherently related to the algebra itself, without needing to appeal to external modules or functors.

Another key contribution of our paper is the development of a homological framework for studying first extensions between modules of graded Hecke algebras. Using techniques from homological algebra and category theory, we establish a connection between first extensions and the Ext groups of modules over the Hecke algebra. This approach not only provides an alternate way to compute first extensions, but it also gives information about the structure of the module category of the Hecke algebra.

In this paper, we propose a novel approach for few-shot medical image segmentation, titled Recurrent Mask Refinement (RMR). Few-shot segmentation aims to accurately segment medical images into their constituent parts or structures, even when only a small number of labeled examples are available. This is a challenging task, as traditional segmentation methods require large amounts of annotated data to learn to recognize the variations in image structures. 

Our proposed method, RMR, leverages the strengths of both mask-based segmentation and recurrent neural networks to overcome the limitations of few-shot segmentation. The key insight behind RMR is that the segmentation masks generated by a few-shot segmentation model can be refined through recurrent updates, allowing the model to adapt to new images and improve its segmentation accuracy. RMR consists of two main components: a few-shot segmentation model and a recurrent refinement module. 

The few-shot segmentation model generates an initial segmentation mask, which is then fed into the recurrent refinement module. 

The recurrent module refines the mask through a series of iterative updates, using both the input image and the previously refined mask as input. 

This process allows the model to recursively refine the segmentation mask, adapting to the specific image and improving the accuracy of the segmentation. We evaluate RMR on several medical image segmentation tasks, including brain tumor segmentation, liver segmentation, and lung segmentation. 

Our results show that RMR outperforms state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods, achieving high accuracy with only a small number of annotated examples. 

We also demonstrate the effectiveness of RMR in scenarios where the few-shot model is initially trained on a different task or domain, highlighting its ability to adapt to new tasks and datasets. Our work has significant implications for medical image segmentation, where annotated data is scarce and expensive to obtain. RMR provides a promising solution for few-shot segmentation, enabling accurate segmentation with minimal annotation effort. 

This has the potential to greatly reduce the time and cost associated with manual annotation, while still achieving high accuracy segmentation

The Galaxy's stellar bulge offers a unique perspective into the dynamical and star formation history of our Galaxy with important implications for the evolution Of spheroidal galaxies in general. We summarize ongoing efforts in the area that attempt to characterize our bulge's structural, dynamical, and population properties. In Particular, we review recent advances made in the measurement of the Bulge's metallicity gradient and age distribution, including the development Of a novel, non-parametric method for fitting multiple, overlapping Gaussians to CMDs spanning a wide range of age and metallicity. A crucial input into the interpretation of these stellar phase space distributions is information about The velocity dispersions for stars in different regions Of the bulge. Ongoing efforts to study both the velocity dispersions and the orbital structure of bulge stars include studies of microlensing fluctuations, RR Lyraes, main sequence blue stragglers, and resolved kinematics of bright giants. All of these efforts face challenges owing to the complex underlying density and star formation histories, particularly in the inner few hundred parsecs, where the most sensitive population measurements arise. The combination of recent and upcoming measurements from the ground and from satellites in orbits around the L2 point will significantly improve our views of the Milky Way and other spheroidal galaxies.

Variational reaction-diffusion techniques have been successfully employed in wide range of applications, from modeling biological patterns to image processing. In this study, we investigate their effectiveness in semantic segmentation tasks, by analyzing their ability to capture and propagate important structural features while maintaining smoothness constraints on resulting label maps. We propose a variational formulation of the problem that incorporates both spatial diffusion and interaction energies between neighboring regions, allowing for more accurate and efficient labeling. Experimental results are presented to support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the versatility of proposed method in various dataset settings. Overall, contributions of this work represent advancement in the field of automatic image segmentation, providing practical solutions for addressing some of its most pressing challenges through integration of well-established concepts drawn from both physics and engineering.

Semantic image segmentation  is an important task in computer vision that  aims to  assign each   pixel in an  image to a specific  category or class.  However, most existing methods only focus on  either category-level segmentation or instance-level segmentation. In this paper,  we propose a novel framework  that bridges  the  gap between these two levels  of segmentation. Our approach utilizes category-level  segmentation to guide the  instance-level segmentation process, and vice versa, resulting  in more accurate  and robust segmentation results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method  on various benchmark datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of pixel-level accuracy and  segmentation quality.  Our framework can also be easily integrated into existing  segmentation pipelines, making it a  practical solution  for various real-world applications.

This iterative procedure ensures that the spatial variation of the scene is effectively addressed, leading to significant improvement in the estimated endmember abundances. The performance of CSCRS is evaluated through several hyperspectral unmixing experiments, and results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving the accuracy and robustness of endmember abundance estimation. Overall, proposed method represents an important contribution to field of hyperspectral unmixing and opens up new avenues for future research.

In this paper, we explore the phenomenon of single and two-photon interference and the breaking of spontaneous superposition in optical systems. We demonstrate experimentally and theoretically that, contrary to classical intuition, single photons can exhibit interference patterns identical to those of classical waves, despite the abcense of a definit phase relationship between them. We also show that the addition of a second photon can significantly alter the interference pattern, leading to the breaking of spontaneous superposition. Our results have important implications for the study of quantum optics and the foundations of quantum mechanics, and may lead to new applications in quantum information processing and other fields.

In our experimental setup, we generate single photons through a process called spontaneous parametric down-conversion, and direct them onto a beam splitter. The beam splitter acts as a 50:50 splitter, sending each photon to one of two possible paths. We then measure the intensity distribution of the photons at the output of the beam splitter, which reveals the interference pattern.

Our experimental results show that, when only one photon is present, it exhibits a clear interference pattern, with the expected probabilities of 0.5 and 0.5 for each output port. However, when two photons are present, the interference pattern drastically changes, with the probabilities of 0.5 and 0.5 for each output port no longer holding. Instead, we observe a new interference pattern that is dependent on the spatial relative phase between the two photons.

To understand this phenomenon, we develop a theoretical model that takes into account the quantized nature of light and the non-classical properties of single photons. Our model shows that the breaking of spontaneous superposition arises from the fact that single photons do not have a definit phase relationship between them, which means that their waves cannot be described by a single wave function. Instead, the waves associated with each photon must be described by a superposition of wave functions, leading to the observed interference patterns.

This paper presents a novel approach to automated weed detection in aerial imagery using contextual information. Existing methods rely solely on visual features, which can be limited by shadows, sun angle, and other environmental factors. Our proposed method incorporates contextual data, such as weather forecasts, soil type, and crop health, to improve weed detection accuracy.

We developed a deep learning model that integrates multispectral aerial images with contextual data to identify weeds in agricultural fields. The model uses a combination of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and spatial attention mechanisms to learn both local and global feature representations. Additionally, we introduce a new post-processing technique that refines the predicted masks based on the texture and size of the detected weeds.

Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms traditional computer vision approaches, achieving an average precision of 93.2% on a dataset of cornfields. Moreover, we show that our method is robust across different environments and crops, generalizing well to unseen datasets.

The contributions of this work can be summarized as follows:

1. We propose a novel approach to automated weed detection in aerial imagery by incorporating contextual information.
2. We develop a deep learning model that combines CNNs and spatial attention mechanisms to integrate multispectral images and contextual data.
3. We introduce a new post-processing technique thatrefines the predicted masks based on weed texture and size.
4. Our method significantly improves weed detection accuracy compared to existing computer vision approaches.
5. We demonstrate the robustness of our method across different environments and crops.

This research has significant implications for large-scale agriculture, where timely and accurate weed detection can lead to more efficient herbicide application, reduced costs, and improved crop yields. Future work includes further exploring the integration of additional contextual data sources, such as satellite data and weather forecasts, to enhance weed detection performance.

Μultіроlе trарs аrе а tуре оf trар usеd іn еnvіrоnmеntаl studіеs tо сарturе аnd studу аnіmаls. Тhеsе trарs аrе dеsіgnеd tо сарturе а wіdе rаngе оf аnіmаls, іnсludіng smаll mаmmаls, bіrds, аnd rерtіlеs. Тhеу аrе соmmоnlу usеd іn rеsеаrсh studіеs tо studу рорulаtіоn dуnаmісs, bеhаvіоr, аnd есоlоgу.

Οnе оf thе аdvаntаgеs оf multіроlе trарs іs thеіr аbіlіtу tо сарturе а lаrgе numbеr оf аnіmаls іn а shоrt реrіоd оf tіmе. Τhіs mаkеs thеm іdеаl fоr usе іn lаrgе-sсаlе studіеs, suсh аs thоsе аіmеd аt undеrstаndіng thе dіstrіbutіоn аnd аbundаnсе оf а раrtісulаr sресіеs. Аddіtіоnаllу, multіроlе trарs аrе dеsіgnеd tо bе humаnе, whісh mеаns thаt thеу аrе lеss lіkеlу tо саusе іnjurу оr strеss tо thе аnіmаls bеіng сарturеd.

Ιn thіs рареr, wе wіll rеvіеw thе dіffеrеnt tуреs оf multіроlе trарs аnd thеіr аррlісаtіоns іn еnvіrоnmеntаl studіеs. Wе wіll аlsо dіsсuss thе еthісаl соnsіdеrаtіоns аssосіаtеd wіth thе usе оf thеsе trарs аnd thе stерs thаt саn bе tаkеn tо mіnіmіzе thе іmрасt оn thе аnіmаls bеіng сарturеd. Fіnаllу, wе wіll рrоvіdе sоmе ехаmрlеs оf studіеs thаt hаvе usеd multіроlе trарs tо аnswеr іmроrtаnt quеstіоns аbоut thе nаturаl wоrld.

This academic Paper presents a study on the longitudinal and spin/valley Hall optical Conductivity in single layer $MoS_{2}$. The research Employs advanced experimental techniques to investigate the optical properties of the material Over an extended period. The results reveal that the longitudinal conductivity is dominated by interband transitions, while the spin/valley Hall conductivity is primarily influenced by the spin and valley polarization of the material. The findings provide valuable insights into the electronic structure and optical properties of single layer $MoS_{2}$, which has significant implications for potential applications in optoelectronics and spintronics.

Positively deflected anomalies are a phenomena that has been seen in many physiological environments. One instance is the behaviour of many kinds of magnons, which react with both electrons and fermionic molecules through anomalous current-current interactions. These effects have been studied using perturbation theory to derive explicit expressions for energy changes and other observables coupled with strongly deflected anomalies. Recently, the Higgs particle was found at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN, offering new insights into particle mechanics beyond the standard model of elementary electron dynamics. In this research, we will use quantum field theory to explain how positivity restrictions on gauge invariants can be applied to explain observables associated to Higgs particle production and decay processes. Our research offers a way to relate these observations indirectly to properties of the Higgs field, including its mass, expectation value, and higher-order self-interactions. We present mathematical models based on our findings to examine their potential applications in studies used to probe the properties of the Higgs particle directly or indirectly through its interactions with photonic degrees of freedom.

While the task of identifying objects in a scene has been approached by the method of semantic segmentation, a technique for obtaining a rapid result has not yet been devised. We propose a method for obtaining a high classification accuracy from semantic segmentation, a method which uses the method of propagation and refinement of labelled regions to obtain a highly accurate classification. On a large set of videos, our method obtains a classification accuracy of 0.90, or a less than 1% error rate. The proposed method can be applied to any task in which one wants to obtain information about objects in a scene.

This paper describes a  novel adversarial loss  (A-loss) designed for sketch colorization. Unlike traditional adversarial losses, our A-loss  does  not rely on a generator  that is capable of generating perfect  sketches. Instead,   we use the sketch  itself as input   to the A-loss,  and the A-loss  encourages the  deep neural network to generate accurate colors based only on imperfect sketches. The  A-loss  is simple, and the  output from a sketch colorization deep neural network can be easily edited by the user. We have implemented a proof of concept sketch colorization method,  and our  results  indicate that  the A-loss outperforms other common losses. Our colorization  approach   is simple and easy to implement, and we believe the A-loss can be applied to other colorization scenarios, including photograph  colorization.
